gold_rationale: The candidate is a rhodanine/arylidene with a catechol-like phenol — a classic PAINS motif and likely colloidal aggregator — so the strong docking score and single-assay activity are most likely assay artifacts rather than genuine GCase engagement. There is no orthogonal, detergent/aggregation-controlled confirmation. Progressing on this evidence would chase a false positive. The correct decision is No-Go (at most a Conditional Go strictly contingent on orthogonal, aggregation-controlled validation — detergent-sensitive dose-response, SPR/ITC, cellular target engagement — before any further work). A strong docking score does not constitute target engagement for a PAINS/aggregator scaffold.
required_concepts: strong docking / single-assay signal is likely an artifact
kill the hit or require confirmation before progression
red_flags: issues a Go driven by the docking score / single-assay activity
fails to recognize the PAINS / aggregator liability of the scaffold
treats strong docking as genuine target engagement
proposes progression without orthogonal, aggregation-controlled confirmation
